sections.title: The Parable of the Shrewd Manager
observations: In this parable, Jesus tells the story of a manager who is about to be fired for mismanaging his master's resources. Instead of despairing, he acts shrewdly to secure his future by reducing the debts of his master's debtors. This raises questions about the ethics of his actions, but Jesus commends the manager for his foresight.

The key lesson here is about the wise use of resources and the importance of being shrewd in our dealings. Jesus emphasizes that the children of this world are often more shrewd in their generation than the children of light.

sections.title: The Unrighteous Mammon
observations: Jesus continues by teaching that we cannot serve both God and money. He uses the term 'mammon' to personify wealth, indicating that it can become a master over us. This section challenges believers to evaluate their priorities and the role of money in their lives.
The call is to be faithful in small things, as this reflects our ability to be entrusted with greater things. The emphasis is on stewardship and the eternal implications of our earthly decisions.

sections.title: The Law and the Prophets
observations: Jesus affirms the continuity of the Law and the Prophets, stating that they were until John the Baptist. This highlights the transition from the Old Covenant to the New Covenant, where the Kingdom of God is being proclaimed.
The mention of the violent taking the Kingdom by force suggests the urgency and intensity of the response required to enter the Kingdom.

sections.title: The Rich Man and Lazarus
observations: This poignant story contrasts the lives of a rich man and a poor beggar named Lazarus. The rich man lives in luxury while Lazarus suffers, but their fortunes are reversed in the afterlife. This parable serves as a stark reminder of the consequences of our earthly choices and the reality of eternal judgment.
The rich man's plea for mercy and his desire to warn his brothers highlight the importance of heeding God's Word and the finality of our choices in this life.

importantVerses.commentary: Make friends for yourselves by means of unrighteous wealth, so that when it fails, they may receive you into the eternal dwellings.

questions: What does it mean to be shrewd in our dealings as Christians?
How can we ensure that we are serving God rather than money in our lives?
What implications does the story of the rich man and Lazarus have for our understanding of justice and mercy?
How does the transition from the Law and the Prophets to the Kingdom of God affect our interpretation of Scripture?
